title: Optimal 3D Chemical Recovery with Multimodal Electron Tomography
content: The understanding of material structure, stoichiometry, and chemical distributions in three dimensions (3D) is critical in modern nanomaterial science [1]. 3D volumetric chemistry can be recovered at high resolution by fusing sparse inelastic scattering signals with abundant elastic scattering signals [2]. The fusion of data, as opposed to conventional correlation, uses a physical prior to link imaging modalities and recover new information [3-5]. Multimodal electron tomography (MM-ET) leverages data fusion to break the traditional dose-resolution tradeoff, improving resolution and allowing a more delicate class of materials to be reconstructed with high chemical contrast.
